off_axis_angle.quote: Both detectors are centered 14.6 mrad off the beam axis and receive a narrow-band neutrino flux peaked at 1.8 GeV.

overburden.quote: underground at Fermilab, with 22 meters water equivalent overburden

total_mass.note: Conflict: NOvA PRD 106, 032004 describes the near detector as "290 ton"; the NOvA public page and the 2025 monopole paper say 300 t / 0.3 kt.
total_mass.quote: The 0.3 kt Near Detector is located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target and 100 m underground at Fermilab

summary.plain: A small copy of the NOvA far detector, about 300 tonnes, sitting underground at Fermilab a kilometre from where the neutrino beam is made. It measures the beam before the neutrinos have had time to change type.
summary.technical: Functionally identical 0.3 kt PVC-cell liquid-scintillator tracking calorimeter 1 km downstream of the NuMI target and 100 m underground at Fermilab, on the same 14.6 mrad off-axis line as the far detector.

technology.quote: Charged particle tracking is accomplished via PVC cells filled with a mineral oil-based liquid scintillator.
technology.value: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, functionally identical to the far detector
